fields.claim_quote: Hence, in $\bar{G}$, each vertex is adjacent to all the vertices in the other set, and will not be adjacent to any vertex in the same set as it. in other words, $\bar{G}$ is a complete bipartite graph
fields.explanation: No G-edge crosses the partition, so every cross pair is an edge of the complement. This does not preclude edges within a part: a pair nonadjacent in G becomes adjacent in the complement. For the empty three-vertex graph, edge {1,2} lies inside V2 and witnesses the failure of the claimed equality with the partition's complete bipartite graph. The true statement that a disconnected graph has connected complement is outside this local refutation.
fields.flaw: The proof asserts that for a disconnected G partitioned into V1, V2 with no edges between them, in the complement each vertex is adjacent to NO vertex of its own side, so that the complement is exactly a complete bipartite graph. This intermediate structural claim is false: non-adjacent pairs inside V1 (or V2) in G become edges inside the same side in the complement, so the complement need not be (complete) bipartite.
fields.problem: Complement of a Disconnected Graph is Connected
fields.source_context:
0001 | Let $G$ be a disconnected graph. Prove that its complement $\bar{G}$ is connected.
0002 | 
0003 | I would like to check if my proof of the above (rather famous) problem is valid. It is as follows:
0004 | 
0005 | Since $G$ is disconnected, its vertex set can be partitioned into $2$ disjoint vertex sets, $V_1$ and $V_2,$  such that each vertex is only adjacent to vertices in the same set as it. Hence, in $\bar{G}$, each vertex is adjacent to all the vertices in the other set, and will not be adjacent to any vertex in the same set as it. in other words, $\bar{G}$ is a complete bipartite graph, which is clearly connected, so we are done.
fields.witness: Let G be the empty graph on {0,1,2}, with partition V1={0} and V2={1,2}. G is disconnected and has no edge between the parts. Its complement is K3 and contains edge {1,2} inside V2, whereas the complete bipartite graph for this partition has only edges {0,1},{0,2}. Thus these graphs differ, exactly as the selected Lean theorem establishes.

scope_metadata.source_kind: Proof-check question about a local structural step
scope_metadata.target_scope: The complement need not equal the complete bipartite graph determined by the chosen partition. The final connectivity theorem is not refuted.
